defects.summary: The Insights page exists but no nav item, tab or link points to it, so users can only reach it by typing the URL.
People and access are spread over /people, /settings/members and the project Team tab, so a user cannot tell where to find or manage a teammate or their role.
My tasks is a standalone top-level page showing the same task list that the project Tasks view already narrows with its assignee=me filter.
The CSV import for projects and tasks lives at /docs/import, so a user looking for data import in Settings will not find it.
The project Timeline tab links to /projects/<id>/timeline, which has no page, so clicking it gives a 404.
The Home nav item links to /dashboard, which redirects to /overview, which redirects to /home, so every Home click takes two hops and Home never shows as active.
Task assignee links open /people?person=<id> while the directory opens /people/<id>, so the same person is addressed by query on one route and by path on another.
personUrl builds /people/<handle> but the route looks people up by id, so the assignee link on task detail, the task modal and the Team tab all 404.
Middleware sends signed-out visitors to /sign-in?next=<path> but the sign-in page ignores next and always lands on /projects, so a shared deep link is lost.
The intercepted task modal closes with router.back(); opening the task URL directly or refreshing renders the full page whose Close button also calls back(), which leaves the app or does nothing.
The workspace switcher stores its choice only as ?ws= on the current URL; left nav, tab and in-page links drop it, so the next click silently returns to the first workspace.

The left nav marks items active by exact path match while the settings sub-nav uses prefix match, so on /projects/<id> nothing is active in the left nav and on /settings/members both Profile and Members look active.
The project Docs tab links to the global /docs, so the user leaves the project, loses the project header and tabs, and the left nav context changes.
On a narrow screen the mobile menu panel stays open after a link is tapped because its open state is never reset on navigation, covering the new page.
The Tasks status filter is local component state, so it resets on refresh, Back or when the link is shared.
The task search text is kept in a module-level variable shared by all projects, so a query typed in one project pre-fills the search box in another.
The Invite dialog opens with router.replace and closes with router.push, so Back cannot close it (it leaves the page) and after closing, Back reopens it.
Project tabs navigate with replace, so switching tabs adds no history entries and Back jumps out of the project instead of returning to the previous tab.
